Dlock 1.0.1

Version 1.0.1 · Build 15 · November 10, 2026

This update adds clearer feedback while Dlock moves your Dock, protects placement from accidental input, and introduces an opt-in workaround for keeping a side Dock on a chosen display. It also brings profile, reconnect, notification, and automation improvements introduced since version 1.0.0 build 7.

A clearer experience while moving the Dock

  • A full-screen processing overlay now makes it clear when a Dock move is in progress.
  • Each connected display uses its own desktop wallpaper as the source of the overlay's colors.
  • A soft, full-screen blur, enlarged wallpaper crop, and subtle dark veil keep the processing message readable.
  • The new Quiet focus layout uses a centered app icon and message without an enclosing card.
  • A smaller heading keeps the screen calm and leaves more space around the content.
  • The app icon is resolved by macOS from Dlock's bundled icon instead of using a fixed exported image.
  • The icon follows the application's system appearance independently of the overlay's dark background.
  • A nine-dot circular activity indicator animates in a chevron wave while work continues.
  • Shimmering status text distinguishes preparation, movement, and placement verification.
  • An elapsed timer shows how long the current move has been running, synchronized across displays.
  • Reduce Motion keeps the activity dots and status text static while the timer continues to update.

Placement that tolerates accidental input

  • Incidental pointer movement no longer cancels an app-initiated Dock move while the processing shield is active.
  • Pointer clicks, scrolling, and ordinary keyboard actions are briefly suppressed during protected placement so they do not act on an unintended target.
  • Dlock's own marked placement events continue to reach the system Dock.
  • Press Escape to request cancellation and let Dlock finish its cleanup safely.
  • Command–Option–Escape remains available during protected placement.
  • An independent 12-second timeout releases the processing shield if a placement stops returning normally.
  • Placement waits for the initiating mouse click to finish before protecting input.
  • Overlay windows are removed on completion and cancellation, including when a display-change callback was already queued.
  • Temporary auto-hide shortcuts are marked as Dlock events so the input shield does not block its own cleanup.

Optional Side Dock Mode

  • Added a session-only, opt-in workaround for Left and Right Dock placement on a selected display.
  • Side Dock Mode temporarily makes the selected display the main display while retaining the monitors' relative positions.
  • Dlock checks the observed Dock location before reporting that placement succeeded.
  • The original configuration is recorded before a display change so recovery can be attempted after an interrupted operation.
  • Original display setup restoration is available when leaving the mode, unlocking, selecting Bottom, quitting, or recovering from a failed move.
  • Settings includes Restore Original Display Setup and a way to keep the current setup when recovery needs a decision.
  • Recovery checks for user layout changes and disconnected or changed displays before restoring a saved configuration.

Side Dock Mode changes which screen is the main display. macOS still controls side-Dock placement, and some interior or covered edges cannot host it. The workaround has been exercised on the connected built-in/HP E233 setup; behavior across every display arrangement is not claimed.

Profiles, reconnects, and controls

  • Added a configurable fallback-display policy for when the preferred display disconnects.
  • Improved setup-aware profile restoration for matching connected-display sets.
  • Added profile archive support for importing and exporting saved setups.
  • Improved restoration of Dock preferences associated with a saved profile.
  • Simplified the visible Dock lock controls around the supported size-lock workflow.
  • Added more explicit restoration and reconnect feedback so users can understand the current preferred and observed display state.

Notifications and automation

  • Routed Dock feedback through native macOS notifications.
  • Added distinct status symbols and colors for success, warning, and error feedback.
  • Added native Shortcuts actions for opening controls, changing the display lock, setting the Dock edge or auto-hide, applying saved profiles, and supported Dock-setting locks.
  • Added a Dock automation request path with input validation and clear failure responses.

Compatibility and update information

  • Requires macOS 13 or later. Accessibility access is required for Dock protection and placement.
  • The release includes Apple silicon and Intel builds. Intel runtime behavior has not been separately verified.
  • The update is signed with the existing Sparkle update key so current installations can verify it.
  • Display reconnect, sleep/wake, permissions, login behavior, and every possible multi-display arrangement have not all been revalidated for this release.
